correctness.rationale: For all nonconstant rational Pick inputs with nonnegative slope and positive simple-pole residues, the published pi-normalized two-graph formula and alpha=1/J_prime(g) imply inverse-graph Jacobian cancellation. Strict positivity of phi_prime yields all simple real inverse roots. Vieta yields sum roots = sum poles+(s-b)/a for a>0, or sum poles+Gamma/(b-s) for a=0, s!=b. Differentiating gives the claimed density 1/a or Gamma/(b-s)^2. Exceptional points have null projected mass. The zero-slope density has quadratic nonintegrable poles at two real nonzero roots, giving the exact local-finiteness distinction. Rational identity classifies equal marginals; finite intersections of rational graph supports prove mutual singularity. Sympy confirms leading-coefficient signs and included standalone CHECK.py passes fifteen numerical trace probes, which are explicitly non-proofs.

originality.rationale: The 2026 source proves individual extremality and its full graph representation, and the first projection follows already from that material; none of these is claimed as novel. The new theorem compares full two-projection data across arbitrary rational inputs, requiring the inverse-first-coordinate Vieta trace and a separate singular-fiber argument; no inspected source states or immediately specializes to this two-marginal equivalence classification. The 2024 hyperplane theorem and 2023 general Clark structure formulas are distinguished by support geometry and uncomputed marginal classes. Indexing limitations and the possibility of an equivalent prior result are acknowledged.
residual_risks: A differently worded inverse-root trace or two-projection equivalence theorem may exist in older Clark or Herglotz literature that was not retrieved by accessible indexing.

value.rationale: The second marginal is a natural observable for recovering an extremal two-dimensional representing measure, and all parameters and arbitrary pole counts are covered. The theorem identifies the exact analytic cutoff a=0 between locally finite Lebesgue and non-locally-finite second projections, classifies complete equivalence fibers of the pair of projections, and exhibits continuum families of pairwise singular extreme measures with identical observations. This is a structural classification motivated by uniqueness of inverse reconstruction, not a table recomputation, arbitrary finite slice, or mere normalization check.
